summary: Collapsed the hello-world teaching surface from 1,968 lines across three documents to 469 across two (a 76% reduction), retiring the hand-maintained shared-spine drift discipline outright rather than relocating it. Authored docs/tutorials/hello-world.md - six parts mapping 1:1 to the six planned video scenes, solo-first with an explicit "Solo repositories can stop here." at the end of Part 4, GitHub + GitHub Copilot CLI as the worked path, Azure DevOps and direct-provider-API as inline variants, three-stage branch protection, one minimally-adapted aggregate CI job, and a five-item final check. Authored docs/tutorials/release-and-recovery.md from the excised release/hotfix/rollback part and the Git-under-the-hood appendix, every command re-verified against gitWorkflow.ts and gitRelease.ts rather than inherited from the retired appendix (L-064-8). Deleted the 821-line Copilot+ADO cut and the 390-line workflow review prompt; left one redirect stub and repaired every inbound link outside the three files Session 2 owns. Both named runtime unknowns were resolved EMPIRICALLY before the affected steps were written (s1-runtime-unknowns.md): the shipped module writers were bundled with esbuild and driven against a real-scaffolder fixture, showing Rename Module carries neither folder names, planPath, nor codeRoots - so Part 3 takes the spec's sanctioned New Module + Delete Module fallback; and the Copilot CLI was probed live, confirming --model claude-sonnet-4.6 runs on CLI 1.0.75 while surfacing live catalog version-pin drift against the 1.0.69 lock (router-side, out of scope, flagged to the operator). Verification was unusually productive and every finding was resolved in flight: a routed reader-simulation pass caught 5 issues pre-verification; cross-provider discovery + supplementary caught 13 blocking findings (including a genuinely broken sys.path on 'python services/app/app.py', the Copilot-CLI-vs-Copilot-Chat conflation, and an ADO policy that cannot be set to zero reviewers), all remediated in one pass; remediation-review cycle 1 caught 2 regressions in that remediation - one of them introduced by my own line-count trimming - both fixed; cycle 2 settled the disputed Azure Pipelines finding (the verifier accepted the named-equivalents scope statement, so the operator-confirmed cut list held without an override) and raised one Node.js-floor Major whose stated evidence was checked and found false (npm view @github/copilot reports engines: null) but whose concern was real - fixed by REMOVING the Node prerequisite entirely, after winget list proved the walk machine runs the standalone GitHub.Copilot build with no Node involved. That same check established the CLI self-updates, which is the mechanism behind the pin drift, now taught explicitly. Known deviation, disclosed not hidden: the tutorial is 314 source lines against a spec target of ~240 and an Ends-with of <=260. Every line above the first 269-line draft closed a step a reader could not perform; the overage was not bought back by reversing fixes. S4's live operator walk is the right place to find further cuts.
blockers: OPERATOR ADJUDICATION 1 of 2 (R8-2, size): the tutorial is 344 source lines against the spec's ~240 target and <=260 Ends-with. Every line above the 269-line pre-verification draft was added by a verifier-demanded correctness fix across rounds 1-7; reversing any re-opens a Major. Options in s1-remediation-round-8.md: (1) accept 344 and re-baseline - recommended, the set still delivers 1,968 -> 499 lines, a 75% reduction; (2) cut the ADO and direct-API variants to ~315, which re-opens the round-3 ADO-completeness argument; (3) let S4's live walk find the real cuts.

OPERATOR ADJUDICATION 2 of 2 (R8-1, worktrees): the backstop wants all four doc-writing lifecycle sets wrapped in worktrees. The finding's valid kernel - an over-broad claim in my own prose that no AI session touches the main checkout - was fixed by narrowing the sentence. Accept the narrowed claim, or override the cut list.
